headline: Scientists Unlock 13,000-Year-Old Secrets in Famous French Cave Art
meta_description: Hidden charcoal in black pigments lets scientists finally date prehistoric paintings at Font-de-Gaume cave in France, revealing artwork spanning thousands of y…
summary_short: Researchers discovered charcoal inside ancient black pigments at a French cave, allowing them to date a bison painting to 13,000 years ago and revealing a mysterious mas…
body:
For the first time, scientists have precisely dated mysterious prehistoric paintings inside Font-de-Gaume, a celebrated cave near Les Eyzies in southwestern France. Using advanced imaging techniques, researchers discovered that black pigments long thought to contain only minerals actually held traces of charcoal—organic material that could be radiocarbon dated. A bison painting was created between 13,461 and 13,162 years ago, placing it in the Upper Paleolithic period when anatomically modern humans produced Europe's most renowned cave art. Even more intriguingly, a mask-like figure in the same cave revealed evidence of artistic activity spanning thousands of years, with different sections dated to periods separated by several millennia. This suggests the image was not completed in a single creative session but rather modified and reinterpreted by different communities across vast stretches of time.

The breakthrough came through non-invasive analysis methods. Researchers used Raman microspectrometry and hyperspectral imaging—techniques that examine light and molecular vibrations to identify materials without damaging the artwork. Once charcoal was confirmed, scientists received rare permission to extract tiny samples for carbon-14 testing, minimizing impact on these irreplaceable images.

The discovery transforms how archaeologists understand prehistoric caves. Rather than viewing decorated caves as static snapshots of a single moment, researchers can now see them as layered palimpsests—meaningful places that communities revisited, modified, and reinterpreted across generations. This research opens new pathways for dating and understanding when people entered these sacred spaces, what they created, and how they returned to add new meaning to existing art.
quick_facts: Bison painting dated to between 13,461 and 13,162 years ago
Font-de-Gaume cave located near Les Eyzies in southwestern France
Mask figure shows artwork created across periods separated by thousands of years
Raman microspectrometry and hyperspectral imaging revealed hidden charcoal in pigments
